spectral.true_color: The scene is relatively dark: water is nearly black to blue-green, woody cover is dark green and olive, and narrow openings are brighter green; high confidence. Scattered gray-brown patches interrupt the vegetation; high confidence. No large bright built surface or opaque cloud is apparent; medium confidence.
spectral.false_color: Most land becomes mottled red to dark crimson, while narrow shoreline and interior vegetation bands become vivid pink-red; high confidence. Water remains near-black to dark blue, with a more cyan northern margin in the southeastern water area; high confidence. Muted gray-green patches show weaker vegetation-like contrast; high confidence.

implications.claim: Widespread red supports extensive foliage-bearing vegetation, but relative redness alone does not establish plant health or productivity.
Brighter pink-red bands likely differ from surrounding woody cover in vegetation density, structure, species composition or illumination.
Some bright bands may represent moist low vegetation because they adjoin water and occupy connecting openings.
Dark, smooth areas with low near-infrared response are open water.
The southeastern cyan margin could reflect shallow water, submerged material, suspended matter or shoreline mixing; turbidity cannot be isolated.
Muted gray-brown land patches could contain exposed soil, rock or sparse vegetation; built surfaces are not securely identified.

spectral.not_revealed: These display composites do not establish calibrated reflectance, quantitative vegetation indices, soil moisture, water depth, turbidity, species, crop identity or vegetation health; high confidence. Without shortwave-infrared bands, temporal observations and ancillary information, substrate composition, wetness and disturbance timing remain poorly constrained; high confidence.

interpretation.claim: Agricultural cultivation is not clearly expressed in the visible patch.

interpretation.claim: A possible access corridor indicates limited human modification, but forestry management is unconfirmed.
interpretation.evidence: Level 3: the narrow diagonal line in top_right could be a track; no associated clear-cut geometry or timber infrastructure is resolved.

interpretation.claim: No settlement can be identified reliably.
interpretation.evidence: Levels 2–4: tiny bright spots in middle_right lack resolved building shapes, associated streets or a coherent built footprint.

interpretation.claim: Vegetation is extensive and spectrally heterogeneous, but ecological condition and degradation cannot be established.
interpretation.evidence: Levels 1 and 4: widespread red vegetation with variable brightness across all land cells; no temporal or calibrated health evidence is available.

interpretation.claim: The openings provide insufficient evidence to diagnose active clearing, harvest, irrigation, erosion or flooding.
interpretation.evidence: Levels 2–4: irregular lighter patches and bright vegetation bands have multiple plausible explanations, and no diagnostic machinery, sediment plume, irrigation layout or dated change is visible.

interpretation.claim: A forest–freshwater or forest–wetland biome setting is plausible, but salinity and climate zone are unresolved.
interpretation.evidence: Levels 1–4: wooded shorelines and small water areas are compatible with multiple climatic and hydrological settings; no unique geographic or climatic indicator appears.

summaries.w25: Wooded shores surround western and southeastern water areas (high confidence). Bright vegetation bands may mark wet openings (medium confidence); land management remains unresolved.
summaries.w50: This wooded aquatic mosaic contains approximately 64% woody cover and 23% water (medium confidence). Western water narrows centrally; another water area occupies the southeast (high confidence). Bright red vegetation bands may indicate moist openings (medium confidence). A possible northeastern track is uncertain (low confidence); management and climate remain unresolved.
summaries.w100: The patch is a wooded shoreline mosaic (high confidence), with estimated cover of 64% woody vegetation, 23% water, 9% low vegetation and 4% sparse cover or exposed ground (medium confidence overall). Western water narrows into a passage, while a smaller water area occupies the southeast (high confidence). Vivid false-color vegetation bands cross the lower center and border water; some may be moist openings (medium confidence). A northeastern diagonal corridor could be a track (low confidence). Agriculture, settlement and active disturbance are not securely identified (medium confidence). Exact season, climate and vegetation health remain unresolved (high confidence).
summaries.w200:
A wooded aquatic landscape dominates the patch (high confidence). Visual estimates allocate 64% to woody vegetation, 23% to water, 9% to low vegetation and 4% to sparse cover or exposed ground (medium confidence overall). Open water occupies much of the western edge, narrowing around a western land projection; another irregular water area is cropped by the southeastern boundary (high confidence).

Land has a mottled dark-green appearance in true color and extensive crimson-red response in false color (high confidence). Brighter pink-red strips cross the lower center and follow parts of the eastern and southeastern shores. These likely represent vegetation differing in structure or density, with moist herbaceous cover plausible in some strips (medium confidence).

A diagonal northeastern corridor could be an access track (low confidence). There is no convincing field pattern or settlement footprint (medium confidence). Gray-brown openings cannot be assigned confidently to soil, rock or sparse vegetation (low confidence). The southeastern water's cyan margin has ambiguous causes, including shallow water and mixed shoreline pixels (low confidence). These images cannot establish active flooding, clearing, harvest, ecological health, exact season or climate zone (high confidence).
summaries.w400:
The scene is a wooded shoreline mosaic containing substantial open water (high confidence). Approximate visual cover estimates are 64% woody vegetation, 23% water, 9% low vegetation and 4% sparse vegetation or exposed ground (medium confidence overall). These are interpretive estimates rather than pixel-derived measurements.

Water dominates the northwest and continues down the western edge, constricting around an eastward-projecting land fragment in the middle-left cell (high confidence). Its visible length spans approximately 1.2 km, with widths roughly 100–450 m (medium confidence). A separate visible water area occupies the southeast and extends beyond the lower boundary; its visible footprint is approximately 350 by 300 m (medium confidence). Connectivity between these waters is unresolved (high confidence).

Most central and eastern land is mottled, consistent with woody vegetation (medium confidence). Narrow bright vegetation strips cross the lower center and border the southeastern water, while another strip follows the eastern margin (high confidence). Moist herbaceous vegetation or wetland margins are plausible interpretations of some strips (medium confidence). A diffuse lighter opening occurs near the southwestern bottom edge (medium confidence). A roughly 450–550 m diagonal corridor in the northeast could be an access track, but its function is uncertain (low confidence).

True color shows dark-green and olive vegetation, nearly black water, brighter green strips and scattered gray-brown patches (high confidence). False color shows extensive crimson vegetation with vivid pink-red bands and dark water (high confidence). Redness supports foliage-bearing cover but cannot independently establish health or productivity (high confidence). The southeastern water's cyan northern margin could reflect shallow water, suspended material, submerged cover or mixed pixels (low confidence).

No convincing agricultural parcel system or settlement footprint is apparent (medium confidence). Forestry, crop rotation and active irrigation, harvest, clearing, erosion or flooding cannot be diagnosed from these observations (high confidence). A forest–wetland setting is plausible, but climate, salinity and biome subtype remain uncertain (low confidence). Native 10 m resolution limits interpretation of tiny bright spots, narrow channels, individual trees and small structures (high confidence).
